name: Honey chili-garlic air-fryer chicken & broccoli

source.author: Instagram (English, pasted text)
source.notes: A one-pan air-fryer marinade dish: cubed chicken breast marinated in soy sauce, honey, chili crisp oil and garlic, then air-fried with sliced onion and broccoli. The post itself notes chicken thighs work well as a swap too. The ½ CUP of soy sauce is a large amount of liquid marinade for an air fryer — the method doesn't mention draining before cooking, so macros here ASSUME roughly 70% of the marinade (soy sauce, honey, chili oil, garlic) actually coats/is consumed and the rest stays in the marinating bowl, a reasonable but uncertain split; if you drain more or less than that, sodium and sugar will move accordingly — flag if you want it recalculated. Chili crisp oil taken as a standard jarred chili-crunch product. Estimate.

ingredients.note: thighs work well as a swap per the original post
the dominant sodium source — see notes on assumed consumption

steps: Marinate the cubed chicken with the honey, soy sauce, chili crisp oil and garlic for a few hours.
Toss the marinated chicken into the air fryer along with the onion and broccoli.
Cook at 400°F (≈200°C) for 10–15 min, then serve.

batch_totals.note: Whole dish (4 servings). Genuinely strong protein and fiber (broccoli pulls real weight here), and it's air-fried rather than pan-fried, so fat stays moderate. The ½ cup soy sauce is the clear sodium outlier of this batch — even at the ~70% assumed consumption used here, it's still very high.

him.verdict: A strong, simple weeknight dish — ~36.9 g protein for only 296 kcal (~12.4 g protein per 100 kcal, right at the top of your library) with real fiber from a full 12 oz of broccoli, and it's air-fried, so fat stays low. The one clear issue is sodium: ½ cup of soy sauce is a lot, and even assuming a chunk of it doesn't fully transfer to the food, this still lands as one of the saltier dishes in your rotation. An easy, high-value fix — cut the soy sauce and/or switch to low-sodium, and this becomes an excellent regular rotation candidate.
flags: ~36.9 g protein / 296 kcal (~12.4 g protein per 100 kcal — excellent)
real fiber (~3.2 g/serving) from a full 12 oz of broccoli
air-fried, not pan-fried — fat stays moderate (~7.4 g/serving)
very high sodium (~1,371 mg/serving) — ½ cup soy sauce is the dominant source
quick, simple, one-pan method — easy weeknight fit
suggested_mods: Cut the soy sauce to ¼ cup and use a low-sodium version — the honey and chili oil still carry plenty of flavor
Drain off excess marinade before air-frying rather than tossing it all in — less liquid pooling, crispier result, less sodium consumed
Try the suggested thigh swap for extra juiciness if breast ever comes out dry in the air fryer
A genuinely good candidate for the rotation once the sodium is dialed back

her_preconception.verdict: Broccoli is a real folate and vitamin-C contributor here, alongside solid protein from the chicken — fully cooked, no safety flags. Sodium is the one thing worth moderating in pregnancy more broadly, same note as for him. A good, simple dish otherwise.
prenatal_highlights: folate + vitamin C from a full 12 oz of broccoli
protein (chicken); fully cooked, no safety flags
suggested_mods: Same sodium-reduction mods as for him — worth it in pregnancy generally
This is already one of the better folate sources among the recent additions thanks to the broccoli

cooking_guide: Cut the chicken into even cubes so everything cooks at the same rate in the air fryer.
Marinate for at least a couple of hours if you have time — honey-soy marinades need a bit longer than a quick 15-minute soak to really penetrate.

Before air-frying, consider lifting the chicken out with tongs rather than pouring in all the marinade liquid — a wetter basket means steaming instead of the caramelized edges you want from an air fryer.
Arrange in a single layer, not piled up — air fryers work by circulating hot air, and crowding the basket blocks that and leads to uneven, soggier results.
Check at the 10-minute mark and shake the basket partway through for even browning; pull it as soon as the chicken hits a safe internal temp rather than going the full 15 min by default.
Tip: if you want more crisp, a quick blast at a higher temp for the last 2 minutes helps the honey glaze caramelize without drying out the chicken.
